Nothing in the file says who judges that, what would make category first class, or when it would be revisited. The source is indeed silent. Empty quote is correct for a gap.

Gap checked at numbered claim 3, line 38: "If the grouping becomes a public concept, it is added to the API then" is the whole of it. The file says nothing about how the grouping would appear in the API, on which endpoints, or who decides. Silent as claimed. Holds.

Refuted as worded. The claim says the ruling leaves open what happens to saved addresses in "any environment other than the two shared ones it names, dev and test", but numbered claim 7 at line 44 does cover one more: "locally, the stack is restarted" — the extract records that itself at ruling-paul-2026-11-05-p1-043. The real gap is narrower, so it is restated as missed claim ruling-paul-2026-11-05-p1-050-m1: the file says nothing about any environment beyond dev, test and a local stack (for example perf, pre-production or production).

Gap checked at numbered claim 8, lines 45 to 47: the pickers are told to keep pagination but every parameter and limit given (page, pageSize 1 to 100, default 25) is attributed to the list API. No page size, parameter or control for a picker appears anywhere in the file. Silent as claimed. Holds.

Gap checked at numbered claims 2 and 4, lines 32 to 40: line 39 says role and searchRole stand "in place of" addressType, use and searchUse, but nothing says what the list does when a client still sends the old ones (rejected, ignored or still honoured). The only ignore rule in the file is line 32's address type sent on a stored address, exactly as the statement says. Holds.

Gap checked at line 11 and numbered claim 5, line 41: both cover adding a role only. Nothing in the file covers removing or retiring a role, or an address that holds a role no longer offered. Silent as claimed. Holds.
